questions.passageText: A small community library opened near Chinhoyi. Before it existed, several families shared a few textbooks. The new library contained storybooks, reference books and newspapers. A volunteer organised a reading hour every Wednesday and encouraged learners to discuss what they had read. Within months, parents noticed that children were reading more confidently. The library committee then began a book-donation campaign so the collection could grow.
questions.questionText: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: It describes a practical activity and its benefits
questions.answerGuidance: Answer in a complete sentence when explanation is required.

questions.passageText: Learners at a rural school started a baking project to raise money for library materials. With a teacher's guidance, they calculated costs, followed hygiene rules and kept records. At first, profit was small because ingredients were wasted. The learners reviewed their methods, measured ingredients more carefully and improved storage. By the end of the term, they had raised enough money to buy reading books.

A guided walk later taught the family about wildlife and responsible tourism.

The head teacher thanked the learners for remembering details instead of blaming someone.

questions.passageText: A stream used by several families had become muddy because soil was washing from a bare slope. Learners studying soil conservation suggested planting grass and building small barriers across the slope. Adults helped with the work. After several rains, less soil reached the stream. The improvement showed that vegetation can reduce erosion and encouraged families to discuss other ways of protecting water sources.
